items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-28
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] This is Rip them up Joe, huh? ... [INTERVIEWEE] Buddy did.

ctx.x: Well, see, we used to advertise on back there. Mm-hmm. On Sunday. And, God, you know, saw a little scrap or something like that. Mm-hmm. Well, we never paid no time to that. We'd get off the wagon and go and get our drink and get back on there. And there'd be scrappings going on. We'd pay another and pull off. Whole time, right? Rip them up. Rip them up Joe. Mm-hmm.
This is Rip them up Joe, huh? Where does Rip them up Joe come from, anyhow? Who thought that up?

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-28
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Yeah, and Buddy Manatee. >> [INTERVIEWEE] Buddy Manatee bandit player.

ctx.x: And let's see, who else is in the band? Chester's out there. Chester and Edmund Hall, I think that's the band. And they had Earl Foster singing with them in the picture.

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-28
items.q: Buddy did. ... He's one who got a buddy to do. ... But he drank plenty. He spent, he stripped it, you know, the same as I am, man. So we got on that train, you know.

ctx.x: This is Rip them up Joe, huh? Where does Rip them up Joe come from, anyhow? Who thought that up?

Buddy did, huh? He must have had quite a few novelist buddies. He must have had quite a few novelists. He must have had quite a few novelists. He must have had quite a few novelists. And Dad used to tell me about a tune he had called, Mr. Buddy, Mr. Buddy, Mr. Buddy Petite.
